title: 611. Discrete Mathematics, Counting & Graph Theory: Extracting Coefficients from Generating Functions
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Read a coefficient from an expanded polynomial.
questions.question: What is the coefficient of \(x^2\) in \(3+5x+7x^2+x^3\)?
questions.explanation: The coefficient of \(x^2\) is the number that multiplies \(x^2\), which is \(7\). The number \(5\) multiplies \(x\), so it is the coefficient of \(x^1\).
questions.hint: Find the term that contains the required power.

questions.learningObjective: Extract a coefficient from a power of a binomial.
questions.question: What is the coefficient of \(x^2\) in the expansion of \((1+x)^6\)?
questions.explanation: By the binomial theorem the coefficient of \(x^k\) in \((1+x)^n\) is \(\binom{n}{k}\). Here it is \(\binom{6}{2}=\dfrac{6\cdot 5}{2}=15\). The value \(6\) is \(\binom{6}{1}\), the coefficient of \(x\).
questions.hint: Use the binomial coefficient with the exponent of \(x\) below.

questions.concept: A power of a sum of two powers
questions.learningObjective: Extract a coefficient after substituting a power of the variable.
questions.question: What is the coefficient of \(x^4\) in the expansion of \((1+x^2)^3\)?
questions.explanation: Put \(y=x^2\). Then \((1+y)^3=1+3y+3y^2+y^3\), and \(x^4=y^2\), whose coefficient is \(\binom{3}{2}=3\). Only even powers of \(x\) occur in this expansion.

questions.learningObjective: Extract a coefficient from the square of a trinomial.
questions.question: What is the coefficient of \(x^3\) in the expansion of \((1+x+x^2)^2\)?
questions.explanation: The term \(x^3\) arises from choosing \(x^i\) in the first factor and \(x^j\) in the second with \(i+j=3\) and \(0\le i,j\le 2\). The possibilities are \((1,2)\) and \((2,1)\), so the coefficient is \(2\). The value \(3\) is the coefficient of \(x^2\), which arises from \((0,2)\), \((1,1)\), and \((2,0)\).
questions.hint: List the pairs of exponents, one from each factor, that add up to \(3\).

questions.learningObjective: Extract a coefficient from the geometric series.
questions.question: The series \(\dfrac{1}{1-x}=1+x+x^2+x^3+\cdots\) is the generating function of a sequence. What is the coefficient of \(x^7\)?
questions.explanation: Every power of \(x\) appears in the series with coefficient \(1\), so the coefficient of \(x^7\) is \(1\). The series is the generating function of the constant sequence \(1,1,1,\dots\). The exponent \(7\) is not the coefficient.
questions.hint: Look at the pattern of coefficients in the series.

questions.concept: A geometric series with ratio two
questions.learningObjective: Extract a coefficient from a geometric series with a factor.
questions.question: What is the coefficient of \(x^3\) in the series \(\dfrac{1}{1-2x}=1+2x+(2x)^2+(2x)^3+\cdots\)?
questions.explanation: The term containing \(x^3\) is \((2x)^3=2^3x^3=8x^3\), so the coefficient is \(8\). In general the coefficient of \(x^n\) is \(2^n\). The value \(6=2\cdot 3\) multiplies instead of raising to a power.

questions.concept: The square of the geometric series
questions.learningObjective: Extract a coefficient from the square of the geometric series.
questions.question: What is the coefficient of \(x^4\) in \(\dfrac{1}{(1-x)^2}=\left(1+x+x^2+\cdots\right)^2\)?
questions.explanation: The term \(x^4\) arises from \(x^i\cdot x^j\) with \(i+j=4\) and \(i,j\ge 0\). The possibilities are \(i=0,1,2,3,4\), so the coefficient is \(5\). In general the coefficient of \(x^n\) is \(n+1\).
questions.hint: Count the pairs of nonnegative exponents with sum \(4\).

questions.learningObjective: Extract a coefficient from a product with a power of the variable.
questions.question: What is the coefficient of \(x^5\) in the expansion of \(x^2(1+x)^4\)?
questions.explanation: The factor \(x^2\) raises every exponent by \(2\), so the coefficient of \(x^5\) in the product equals the coefficient of \(x^3\) in \((1+x)^4\), which is \(\binom{4}{3}=4\). The value \(6=\binom{4}{2}\) would be the coefficient of \(x^4\) in the product.
questions.hint: Decide which power of \((1+x)^4\) is needed after the factor \(x^2\) is taken into account.

questions.learningObjective: Extract a coefficient from a power of a binomial with a numerical factor.
questions.question: What is the coefficient of \(x^3\) in the expansion of \((1+2x)^4\)?
questions.explanation: The term with \(x^3\) is \(\binom{4}{3}(2x)^3=4\cdot 8x^3=32x^3\). The value \(4\) is the binomial coefficient alone; it leaves out the factor \(2^3\) that comes with the third power of \(2x\).
questions.hint: The factor \(2\) is raised to the same power as \(x\).

questions.concept: A bounded sum of two parts
questions.learningObjective: Extract a coefficient from the square of a four-term polynomial.
questions.question: What is the coefficient of \(x^4\) in the expansion of \((1+x+x^2+x^3)^2\)?
questions.explanation: The term \(x^4\) arises from exponents \(i\) and \(j\) with \(i+j=4\) and \(0\le i,j\le 3\). The possibilities are \((1,3)\), \((2,2)\), and \((3,1)\), so the coefficient is \(3\). The value \(5\) counts all pairs of nonnegative exponents with sum \(4\), including \((0,4)\) and \((4,0)\), which are not available because no factor contains \(x^4\).
questions.hint: Each factor offers exponents from \(0\) to \(3\) only.
